method: Refero design skill, live Refero reference metadata/flows/images and read-only current source review

fullStyles.title: Asana
fullStyles.northStar: Productivity whiteboard lit by a coral lamp — authoritative black type on a breathing white field, with a warm coral flash and a deep-navy flicker to signal where action lives.
fullStyles.description: Asana reads as a white canvas under a coral-and-violet editorial system — generous whitespace punctuated by a near-black (#0d0d0d) headline weight that commands attention, then released into light gray body copy. The signature move is two coexisting type voices: Ghost at 60-72px with -0.0070em tracking for display headlines that compress letter forms into dense, authoritative blocks, and TWK Lausanne at 300-500 weight handling everything else with a humanist openness. Pill buttons (100px+ radius) float as soft capsules against sharp-cornered cards (10-16px), creating gentle contrast between interaction surfaces and content containers. The coral tint (#ffeaec background, #690031 deep text) acts as a warm semantic accent for the product's brand-colored UI elements, while a saturated dark violet (#222875) marks interactive and informational states — both restrained to small, intentional doses against an otherwise achromatic canvas.

fullStyles.title: Todoist
fullStyles.northStar: Warm, minimal productivity suite. Like a neatly organized desk bathed in natural light.
fullStyles.description: This design system presents a clean, business-casual aesthetic, grounded in warm off-white and charcoal neutrals, punctuated by a signature vibrant red-orange. The generous use of rounded corners (15px for prominent elements, 8px for most others) softens the utilitarian feel of the task manager, while subtle, low-opacity shadows add minimal depth without visual clutter, creating an approachable, yet professional, interface.

fullStyles.title: Ui
fullStyles.northStar: Monochromatic architectural blueprint – precise, functional forms on a stark, bright canvas.
fullStyles.description: This design system feels like a finely tuned machine, presenting a clean and precise interface with a stark black-and-white aesthetic. The visual mood is serious and functional, achieved through a dominant achromatic palette and very subtle elevation. Geometric balance is created by mixing hard 10-14px radii for cards and inputs with highly rounded (near-pill) buttons and badges, suggesting both structure and approachability. The use of a custom sans-serif font across all elements with meticulous letter-spacing creates a unified, crisp typographic voice.

flows.name: Create issue with sub-issue and recurrence

steps.name: Empty Active issues
steps.goal: Start creating a new issue from an empty Active list
steps.action: User clicks the primary 'Create new issue' button in the empty state
steps.systemResponse: Opens the 'New issue' modal centered over the issues list

steps.name: New issue modal opened
steps.goal: Provide title and description for the new issue
steps.action: User focuses the title field and description area in the modal
steps.systemResponse: Blank title/description inputs become active; inline metadata chips (Todo, Priority, Assignee, type) are visible

steps.name: Title and description entered
steps.goal: Capture a concise issue title and supporting description
steps.action: User types 'Improve loading time on dashboard' and a short description
steps.systemResponse: Text populates the modal; action buttons (Create issue / Create more) remain enabled

steps.name: Open priority selector
steps.goal: Choose priority level for the issue
steps.action: User clicks the Priority chip to open the priority dropdown
steps.systemResponse: Priority dropdown appears listing options (No priority, Urgent, High, Medium, Low)

steps.name: Select priority
steps.goal: Apply a priority tag
steps.action: User selects 'Medium' from the priority list
steps.systemResponse: Priority chip updates to show 'Medium' selected

steps.name: Open assignee picker
steps.goal: Assign the issue to a team member
steps.action: User clicks the Assignee chip to open the people picker
steps.systemResponse: Assignee dropdown shows team members, 'No assignee' option, and an 'Invite and assign...' action

steps.name: Assignee hover tooltip
steps.goal: Inspect member details before assigning
steps.action: User hovers over a team member (Miles Hartman) in the picker
steps.systemResponse: Member tooltip appears showing avatar, name, status, and team context

steps.name: Select assignee
steps.goal: Set a specific person as assignee
steps.action: User clicks a team member (nickstwo) to assign
steps.systemResponse: Assignee chip updates to show the selected member

steps.name: Open issue type selector
steps.goal: Categorize the issue (improvement, bug, feature)
steps.action: User clicks the type chip to open the type dropdown
steps.systemResponse: Type dropdown lists available issue types and highlights the chosen one

steps.name: Open due date menu
steps.goal: Set a due date or recurring schedule
steps.action: User clicks the date/clock icon to open date/recurrence options
steps.systemResponse: Menu shows quick options (Custom, Tomorrow, End of week, In one week) and actions (Set due date, Make recurring, Add link, Add sub-issue)

steps.name: Configure recurrence frequency
steps.goal: Specify the recurrence interval
steps.action: User opens the 'repeats every' frequency dropdown to pick the numeric interval
steps.systemResponse: A numeric list appears (1–12) for choosing how many units between recurrences

steps.name: Recurrence options
steps.goal: Finalize recurrence behavior
steps.action: User toggles options such as 'Don't repeat' or adding sub-issues from the recurrence menu
steps.systemResponse: Recurrence selection is applied; modal shows recurrence summary (first due date and repeats settings) and updates action button label to reflect recurring issue creation

steps.name: Expand create sub-issue area
steps.goal: Add nested work items under the parent issue
steps.action: User checks/enables 'Create sub-issue' to reveal sub-issue input fields
steps.systemResponse: Sub-issue title and description inputs appear inside the modal with their own controls and a separate 'Add sub-issue' CTA

steps.name: Add sub-issue content
steps.goal: Provide a specific sub-task for the parent issue
steps.action: User types a sub-issue title 'Audit API response time for dashboard data' and optional description
steps.systemResponse: Sub-issue content is added to the modal and shown under 'Sub-issues' list

steps.name: Attachment controls revealed
steps.goal: Attach files to the sub-issue
steps.action: User clicks the attachment/paperclip control in the sub-issue area
steps.systemResponse: Attachment chooser/tooltip appears offering to attach images, files or videos

steps.name: Upload file in progress
steps.goal: Upload a file into the sub-issue
steps.action: User selects a file; progress bar displays while uploading (document.pdf)
steps.systemResponse: Upload progress indicator runs; file placeholder with name appears inside sub-issue

steps.name: Attachment added
steps.goal: Confirm attachment is attached
steps.action: System completes upload and lists the uploaded file with size
steps.systemResponse: File is shown as attached to the sub-issue with filename and size metadata

steps.name: Add additional attachment
steps.goal: Attach another supporting file
steps.action: User uploads a second file (Another one.pdf)
steps.systemResponse: Second attachment appears below the first in the sub-issue attachments area

steps.name: Review sub-issues list
steps.goal: Verify sub-issue(s) and recurrence before creating
steps.action: User reviews the grouped sub-issue list, metadata chips, and recurrence summary at the bottom of the modal
steps.systemResponse: Modal shows consolidated view: parent title/description, sub-issue(s) listed, recurrence line (first due date, repeats every X weeks), and primary action button updated to 'Create recurring issue'

steps.name: Issue created and list updated
steps.goal: Finalize creation and confirm addition to Active issues
steps.action: User clicks 'Create recurring issue' (or 'Add sub-issue' then create) to submit
steps.systemResponse: Modal closes; Active issues list updates showing the new parent issue and sub-issue entry; a small confirmation/toast appears noting the created issue

steps.name: Project Kanban Board
steps.goal: Review tasks across columns and locate the task to update
steps.action: Scan the To Do / Doing / Done columns and identify the target task; optionally use '+ Add Task' to create a task
steps.systemResponse: Displays the project board for 'Humanity' with task cards grouped into To Do, Doing and Done. Each column shows a numeric badge of item count and each task card shows compact metadata and an action area.

steps.name: Reveal & Trigger Quick Action
steps.goal: Expose the inline 'mark complete' control and activate it
steps.action: Hover over the task card to reveal the quick-action control. Click the check/complete control (tooltip 'Mark as complete' appears on hover).
steps.systemResponse: The control's tooltip appears. Activating the control applies a green check indicator to the task and the column's numeric count updates to reflect the change (visual immediate feedback).

steps.name: Completion Confirmation Snackbar
steps.goal: Confirm completion and provide a reversible option
steps.action: Observe the confirmation snackbar and choose an action: 'View Tasks' to navigate or 'Undo' to revert the completion.
steps.systemResponse: A temporary snackbar appears with message 'Task marked as complete' and action buttons ('View Tasks', 'Undo'). If the user taps Undo, the task's visual completion state and column count revert; otherwise the completed state remains visible in the board.

steps.name: Completed Tasks List
steps.goal: Scan completed tasks and use search/filters to locate specific items.
steps.action: User views the Completed Tasks screen, can type in the search field, toggle filter buttons (All Clients, specific project), select rows, and use pagination or rows-per-page control.
steps.systemResponse: The table displays matching completed tasks with columns (Task Name, Client, Project, List, Labels, Assignees, Completed). Pagination and rows-per-page controls show current range. Filter buttons are visible but not expanded.

steps.name: Project Filter Expanded
steps.goal: Narrow the completed tasks list by selecting a specific project.
steps.action: User clicks the project filter button, opening a dropdown and selecting/deselecting project options (e.g., Humanity, Refero, All Projects).
steps.systemResponse: A dropdown appears showing project options with checkmarks for selected items. The list reflects the selected project scope (in this screenshot the Humanity project is checked) without navigating away.

steps.name: Empty State — No Matches
steps.goal: Handle the case where filters/search return no completed tasks.
steps.action: After applying filters or search terms that produce no results, the user reads the message and can click the View Active Tasks CTA or adjust filters/search again.
steps.systemResponse: The table is replaced with an empty-state panel that explains no matching tasks were found and provides a prominent 'View Active Tasks' button as a suggested next action.

steps.name: Empty To-Do List
steps.goal: Begin creating a new task from the To-Do List.
steps.action: Select the New To-Do entry in the main content area.
steps.systemResponse: An inline task composer opens with fields for a task name and additional notes, plus controls for task metadata and Cancel and Done actions.

steps.name: Open Task Composer
steps.goal: Prepare the task entry form for input.
steps.action: Enter the task title and supporting notes in the composer.
steps.systemResponse: The composer remains open and accepts the entered task content.

steps.name: Enter Task Details
steps.goal: Record the task and explain what needs to be done.
steps.action: Type the title "Review incoming emails and client messages" and the notes "Check updates from contractors, suppliers, and clients, and reply to urgent inquiries."
steps.systemResponse: The entered title and notes are displayed in the inline editor. The task is not yet saved.

steps.name: Set Due Date
steps.goal: Add a deadline to the task.
steps.action: Use the date control in the composer and select 15 Aug 2026.
steps.systemResponse: The selected date, "15 Aug 2026," appears in the composer alongside the task metadata controls.

steps.name: Assign Task
steps.goal: Identify the person responsible for the task.
steps.action: Use the assignee control and select the user represented by the "L" avatar.
steps.systemResponse: The assignee indicator changes to show the selected user while the task remains in edit mode.

steps.name: Save Task
steps.goal: Finish creating the task.
steps.action: Select Done.
steps.systemResponse: The editor closes and the new task appears in the To-Do List with its title, the 15 Aug due date, and the L assignee indicator. A new New To-Do entry remains available for creating another task.

boundaries: Recommendations only; no application source/runtime/database changed; no application tests rerun. Reference annotations may contain inference; only explicit observed patterns are adopted.
